source_note: Project-context export of the substantive conversation visible in this session. This is not a platform-generated immutable transcript and excludes hidden chain-of-thought.
purpose: Preserve the reasoning needed to resume the Product Vision/System Intelligence work from a fresh chat.

turns.content: While the System Intelligence archaeology is running, identify useful work that can be done without conflicting with it.
Recommended focusing on the first real VIVIM experience and executable product acceptance while avoiding new internal architecture decisions.
Basically V1 should cover at least what vivim old can do.
Clarified that V1 should preserve the meaningful behavioral capability floor of old VIVIM while allowing the new architecture to replace old mechanisms.

Raised self-evolving data model including artifacts/documents; provider abstraction for similar-but-not-identical providers; onboarding/maintenance/self-healing/parsing; provider protocol data stores/use; routing; resource-efficient Chrome master/slave; shared vs bespoke; plugin infrastructure for cross-sharing; self-knowledge; and maximum reprogrammability.
Organized those concerns as likely high-effort V1 design/engineering areas and said the archaeology should expose them as critical paths, boundary risks, unknowns and open frontier.
Asked to anticipate what the first archaeology pass will output and design a second pass to cover what was missed structurally.

Defined Pass 2 as an adversarial structural coverage audit aimed at hidden dependencies, runtime/data flows, evolution limits, provider system, browser substrate, plugin graph, self-knowledge, reprogrammability, legacy parity and boundaries.

Reported 6/6 investigators, 44 atoms, 65 edges, 99 evidence records, 42/42 role artifacts and 11/11 synthesis artifacts. Highlighted the Vault/Evidence → Law/Authority → Recipe/Composition → Intent → Execution/Context spine and Provider → Account → Session → Browser → Realization → Routing → Governed Effect → Evidence chain.

Inspected Wave 1 outputs and concluded that the major seams are visible, but the model is too coarse to answer the hardest questions about data evolution, provider protocol/healing, browser resources, plugin graph, self-knowledge and reprogrammability. Recommended Pass 2 before deep dives.
Requested that AGENTS_CONTEXT/PRODUCT_VISION be updated, with an export of this conversation and a full handoff so a fresh chat can continue from here.

current_decisions: Wave 1 is a map, not a complete structural model.
Pass 2 should falsify Wave 1 before broad implementation or all deep dives.
V1 must preserve the meaningful capability floor of Legacy VIVIM.
The hardest V1 risks are data evolution, provider abstraction/protocol/healing, routing, Chrome substrate, shared-vs-bespoke, plugin composability, self-knowledge and reprogrammability.
immediate_next_action: Let Pass 2 finish; then review V1 Critical Areas and select targeted design/experiment/implementation work.
